feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. The evidence is iteration 4 (58.5, best; wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.08 m), iteration 5 (wheel_radius 0.04 m, 41.4, with s-bend progress falling from 0.185 to 0.0625) and iteration 6 (mass 1.0 kg, 42.7, with s-bend progress at 0.065). Both speed-raising and inertia-raising changes cut usable progress, so overshoot at speed looks like the limit. I kept the iteration 4 controller so your wheel_radius change is isolated, which also lowers effective yaw gain by about 17 percent. When the race reports: if max_error or steering_oscillation falls on the s-bend and slalom while progress holds near 0.185, the overshoot limit is confirmed. If progress falls below about 0.12 on the s-bend, the robot is too slow for the course, so the radius should stay near 0.03 m.
requested_changes: If max_error and steering_oscillation fall on the s-bend and slalom while progress holds at or above 0.18: try wheel_radius 0.02 m (the contract minimum) with wheel_track 0.08 m. Evidence: iteration 5 showed that larger radius cut progress, so the downward direction is the one still untested.

If progress falls below about 0.12 on the s-bend with no drop in max_error: return wheel_radius to 0.03 m and test mass 0.6 kg at that radius. Evidence: iteration 6 (mass 1.0 kg) also cut s-bend progress to 0.065, so mass is the other lever to check with speed held constant.

Do not move the sensors back to y=0.07 m or return wheel_track to 0.12 m. Evidence: iteration 2 (y=0.07 with a lighter body) scored 47.8, and iteration 1 (wheel_track 0.12 m) scored 55.1, both below iteration 4.
